    Unofficial, not affiliated with Mercedes-Benz. Exhibits rotate, so a car may be away when you visit. 3D: three.js (MIT). Headlines: Instrument Serif (SIL OFL).

# Under the skin — a visitor’s review

**8/10 as a museum companion.** At the 300 SL, I could see the open doors in the photograph, cut down the frame for conventional doors, and watch it twist. That experiment gives me a reason to look back at the real car. The harder part is finding the right stop from the gallery floor and knowing which of the moving numbers deserves my attention.

I would fund two changes first. Give visitors a shortcut to the room they are standing in, and put each mechanism’s most revealing experiment beside its first control. The tour already has enough exhibits and engineering detail.

| Part of the visit | Rating | What earns or costs points |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recognizing the car and finding its stop | 6/10 | All 46 stops have a photo, and the cards are grouped by room. On a 393 × 659 phone viewport, Legend 6 began about 32 screen heights down the index. Looking for “Gullwing” in the English card text found the SLS AMG and missed the 300 SL. |
| Learning from the exhibit | 9/10 | The pinned model stays visible while I change the frame or open the SLK roof. I can test a prediction and see the answer. On the Gullwing, the paragraph connecting the frame to the doors was below the visible screen after I tapped the comparison. |
| Choosing how deeply to explore | 7/10 | One mechanism is enough for a satisfying stop, and 34 of the 46 stops have just one. Even a single mechanism can present controls, units, a legend and several facts before I know what to watch. |
| Using the tour between galleries | 9/10 | English and Hungarian, named previous/next links and offline access make it practical to carry. After “Ready offline” appeared, I disconnected Chromium and opened a previously unvisited Evolution II stop. Its model animated. |

## What to change first

1. **Give the index two useful shortcuts.** Keep “See the route.” Add “Three highlights” beside it, linking to the existing three-car tour, and a return link from the highlights to the full route. At the start of the route, add “Jump to a room” using the 11 existing room headings and their levels. Native fragment links can do the work. Include familiar names such as “300 SL Gullwing” in card text so the browser’s Find command works too. A visitor arriving at Level 3 should be able to go straight to Legend 6 and still see the photo cards that help identify the car. [Route page](../index.html) · [Room order](../stops/tour.js) · [Highlights](../teaser.html)

2. **Give each car one memorable question.** Use the route card to pose it, the photograph to show where to look, and the first mechanism to let the visitor discover the answer. Group the remaining material by the follow-up question it answers. The proposed flow and three worked examples follow below.

3. **Make the first photograph useful immediately.** The shared story currently creates a hidden image and reveals it after the 3D viewer initializes. A rendering failure can therefore leave someone standing at the car with an error message and the identifying photo hidden. Show the existing photo, its credit and the takeaway as soon as the story appears. Keep them readable if 3D fails. Also change the index invitation to “Scroll to see where the mechanism sits” so it describes the gesture the tour actually uses. [Viewer](../lib/app/viewer.js) · [Story layout](../lib/app/story.js)

## How a visitor should move through one car

The current route card often tells the story twice. On the 300 SL, the summary explains the doors and introduces fuel injection, then the blue pill lists “Space frame · Engine.” Both lead to the same page. Inside, the visitor encounters the experiment, five readouts, a colour key and finally the facts that explain the doors. The most useful edit is to move the answer closer to the moment the visitor can see it. [Route cards](../lib/app/index.js) · [Frame controls](../subsystems/space-frame.js)

| Moment | What the visitor sees | What belongs here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Choosing from the route | Photo, familiar car name, year and one invitation | Use the room heading for location. Make the card one link. For the 300 SL, “Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Gullwing” and “Why do its doors open upwards?” are enough to choose it. Drop the repeated list of mechanisms from the pill. |
| Standing beside the car | The photo and one thing to find on the exhibit | Give the eye a destination. “Look at the high sill beneath the open door. Imagine climbing over it.” Save the explanation for the moment the frame is visible. |
| Trying the mechanism | A short prompt, the existing control and the result it changes | Group by action. Keep a comparison with its outcome, a sequence with its active phase, or an animation with the part to watch. Keep pause or replay within reach. Use a number only when it helps the visitor see the difference. |
| Deciding whether to linger | The consequence in one sentence, followed by a clearly named disclosure | Let someone leave knowing why the feature matters. Someone who wants the evidence can open “Frame loads and stiffness” right there. Keep units, model qualifications and any essential colour key beside the result they explain. |
| Looking back at the exhibit | The existing closing photo, one observation to take back to the car, then the next-stop link | On the Gullwing, come back to the metal the passenger must step over. Keep production history, sources and detailed assumptions available in the background. |

Each moment fits within the existing scroll. On a phone, the test is whether the visitor can see the model respond and understand the result before the next swipe. A detail disclosure belongs inside its mechanism’s step so opening it keeps that mechanism on the stage. [Shared story layout](../lib/app/story.js)

### Three ways to tell the story

**SLK · One mechanism, told as a sequence.** The route card can ask “Where does a steel roof go when you open it?” On the stop photo, draw attention to the join between roof and rear window. At the model, ask “Which moves first, the boot lid or the roof?” Put “Open the roof” beside the phase indicator. As the lid rises and the two roof pieces fold together, the visitor has the answer. End with the space the owner gives up. The folded roof takes up part of the boot. Put the three angle readings and hinge colours under “How the roof folds.” Keep the reference-photo caption at the image. A visitor can enjoy this whole stop without reading an angle. [SLK story](../stops/slk/car.js) · [Roof controls](../subsystems/vario-roof.js)

**300 SL Gullwing · Two mechanisms, joined by the shape of the car.** Give the frame the first experiment and a natural stopping point. The engine earns its own short chapter through a second feature the visitor can see. [300 SL story](../stops/300sl/car.js)

| What appears in the scroll | Proposed visitor-facing content | Where the depth goes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| At the high sill | “What would happen if those tubes were low enough for an ordinary door?” Keep the two frame choices together, with relative stiffness directly underneath. | Under “Frame loads and stiffness,” keep wheel load, twist angle, stiffness in N·m per degree and tube force. |
| Immediately after the comparison | “With the sides cut down, this model keeps about a third of its stiffness. The tall tubes give the real car its high sill, so the doors hinge from the roof.” | Keep the simplified-model qualification with the 35% result. Put the racing-frame history with the background. |
| Moving from door to bonnet | “Now follow the bonnet towards the nose. How did a tall six-cylinder engine fit under that low line?” Show its lean in the existing model. The 45° lean to the left explains the low bonnet. | Under “Fuel injection and engine timing,” group the invitation to watch the spray with slow motion, firing order and crank/cam readings. The visitor who came for the doors can move on after the frame. |

**540 K · Three mechanisms, told as one drive.** Stage the existing chapters in driving order. **Over a bump**, watch the left front wheel rise and the tyre-load trace change. Keep the trace key beside it and tuck the wheel-angle and track-width figures under “Front suspension geometry.” **On the straight**, use “Floor it” and watch the supercharger clutch engage. The clutch state answers when the extra power arrives. Rotor speed and illustrative boost belong together under “Inside the blower.” **At speed**, hold engine power constant and compare the Cabriolet B with the 1938 Streamliner. Keep the body choice and modeled top speed together, with the wind-tunnel fields available under “Where the drag comes from.” Identify the photographed Cabriolet and the Streamliner comparison where the body choice appears. This gives each swipe a reason even for someone unfamiliar with the term *Kompressor*. [540 K story](../stops/540k/car.js) · [Blower controls](../subsystems/roots-blower.js) · [Aerodynamics controls](../subsystems/aero.js)

### Pilot the grouping before editing all 46 stops

Start with these three cars. For each component, an editor should be able to finish the sentence “When I ___, I can see ___, which matters because ___.” Move the existing control, observation and shortest accurate explanation together. Give remaining material a title a curious visitor would actually open. Translate the complete prompts into Hungarian and check their wrapping below the pinned stage. The same content should work on the car’s own page and wherever it appears in the highlights.

Use the existing panels and native disclosures. Opening a detail should preserve the selected setting, current animation state and scroll context. Reuse the live readout in its new position so a measurement updates only once. In the pilot, ask a casual visitor to explain the Gullwing doors with all details closed, then ask an enthusiast to find the twist angle without losing the selected frame. Both paths should feel complete.

## What information is missing?

**For a short visit, the missing information is where to look.** Across the tour, 59 component stories already contain 229 technical talking points. The opening question, one visible feature of the real exhibit, and the consequence for its driver or passenger have more value on the first screen than another specification. Keep generous depth for enthusiasts, especially the comparisons, sources and clearly identified model assumptions.

**For finding a car, visitors need to know how closely the photo and location match.** The SLK already has a photo, but it shows a street car in Washington, D.C. That explanation comes in the background, after the interaction. Put “Reference photo of the same generation” beside the image. For uncertain rooms, put a brief qualifier next to the room name until someone has checked the exhibit on site. Start with Collection 4 and the 220 S. A gallery check here is worth more than drawing a precise floor map from uncertain locations. [SLK photo note](../stops/slk/car.js) · [Open location questions](../AGENTS.md)

## How to decide whether the changes work

- **Try the pilot on the floor.** Ask five first-time visitors to find a car from its room sign, choose a short visit from the home page, then use the Gullwing comparison and explain the door shape in their own words. A proposed pass is four of five completing each task unaided. Watch where they look back at the car and whether anyone who wants the figures can still find them.
- **Compare on the same phone before and after.** On a physical iPhone, repeat cold opens of the route and the Gullwing under the same network conditions. Record time to usable route links, first visible photo and first working control. Compare frame times while orbiting and changing a control on the Blitzen-Benz wind tunnel. Recheck on iPad and with reduced motion, VoiceOver and Hungarian labels. Investigate any repeatable slowdown before rollout.
- **Protect offline use.** The reviewed build packaged about 9.7 MiB of uncompressed assets. The proposed shortcuts and copy can reuse the current photos and models, add zero new media requests, and keep 3D off the index’s rendering path. After “Ready offline,” repeat the room jump, highlights link and an unseen stop in airplane mode. The existing offline test is a starting point. [Build](../tools/build.mjs) · [Offline test](../tests/e2e/offline.spec.mjs)

*Review basis, 18 November 2026.* I reviewed the route and content inventory at revision `59b1e58`, walked the index, Gullwing comparison, SLK roof control, language switch and highlights in iPhone-sized WebKit, and checked offline entry in Chromium. The ratings are editorial judgments. Actual gallery locations, visitor comprehension and physical-device timing still need field checks.

# Mercedes-Benz Museum technical tour

Static GitHub Pages site: one page per exhibit showing its mechanism working (three.js), offline after one visit, for
iPhone/iPad Safari (iOS 16.4+, import maps). No bundler: native ES modules; `tools/build.mjs` only stamps the service worker.

## Map
- `index.html` route (lib/app/index.js) · `stop.html?s=<slug>[&r=teaser]` one stop as a scroll story (lib/app/shell.js;
  r=teaser pages among the teaser stops and links back to teaser.html): the car's stage pins while its steps (intro on the
  photo, one per component with its cards, background with the outline) scroll past and set what it shows ·
  `teaser.html` the three `teaser` stops' stories one after another (lib/app/teaser.js, own manifest) · `sw.js` offline
  cache (new root files also go in tools/build.mjs ENTRIES)
- `stops/tour.js` route order, room, level, and `teaser` (slugs): single source for order and prev/next ·
  `stops/<slug>/car.js` pure data (+ photo.jpg)
- `lib/model/` pure maths, Node-tested: linkage (multi-link closure), quarter-car (ride), engine (N-cylinder slider-crank,
  timing, diesel), blower, valvetrain (spring float, desmo), steering (double-pivot trapezoid, centre pivot, twin steered
  axles), differential (one axle; traction4: four-wheel drive with locks or brake traction control), gearbox (sliding
  gears), aero (drag, top speed), truss (space frame twist), crash, air-spring (levelling: air, or a motor-wound torsion
  bar), wankel, cooling, belt (two-speed flat-belt drive, hill climbing), hoist (car-transporter deck: cylinder, pulley

I’d fix the room navigation and the Hungarian control labels first. **“See the route” scrolls past the room picker, and two Hungarian labels on the SLK overlap precisely when the visitor needs to follow the roof animation.** The 300 SL offers a good pattern to keep. Its question about the doors gives visitors something to look for on the real car and a reason to try the model.

I reviewed all 46 route cards in both languages and tested the route, highlights, SLK roof and 300 SL frame comparison in WebKit at iPhone and iPad sizes. These are findings from the current local build and device emulation.

### Wording I’d change

The Hungarian works well when it names a part and gives the visitor one thing to watch. It gets harder to follow where it carries over an English metaphor or leaves out the thing being described.

| Where | Current wording and why it trips | Suggested English | Suggested Hungarian |
|---|---|---|---|
| 540 K route card | “When did it join in?” / “Mikor lépett működésbe?” Grammatically, *it* refers to the letter K. | “What does the K stand for? When does the supercharger kick in?” | „Mit jelent a K betű? Mikor kapcsol be a kompresszor?” |
| 300 SL frame buttons | “Lecsökkentve szokásos ajtókhoz” leaves the visitor guessing what was lowered. The two choices should name the visible difference. | “Original high sill” / “Lower sill for conventional doors” | „Eredeti, magas küszöb” / „Alacsony küszöb hagyományos ajtóhoz” |
| SLK roof prompt | “Watch the steps light up” becomes „figyelje, ahogy a lépések kigyulladnak”. *Kigyulladnak* can suggest catching fire. The interesting part is which panel moves first. | “Tap ‘Open the roof’. Which moves first, the boot lid or the roof?” | „Koppintson a „Tető nyitása” gombra. Mi mozdul meg először, a csomagtartó fedele vagy a tető?” |
| Simplex gearbox legend | „Kapcsolódó kerékpár” readily reads as “a connecting bicycle”. The English “pair in mesh” also assumes the visitor knows which parts form the pair. | “Gears in mesh” | „Kapcsolódó fogaskerekek” |
| Offline instructions | “Open this page once with signal” / „nyissa meg … térerővel” suggests mobile reception and gives no clear moment when it is safe to disconnect. | “Open the tour while you’re online. When you see ‘Ready offline’, every stop is saved on this device.” | „Nyissa meg a túrát, amíg van internetkapcsolata. Ha megjelenik »A túra offline is elérhető« üzenet, már az összes megállót elmentette a készülék.” |

One route card also changes the engineering meaning in **both** languages. The Benz Victoria says both front wheels follow the same circle. The inner wheel follows a tighter arc, which is exactly what the model lets visitors see. I’d make that the question: **“Why does the inner front wheel turn more sharply?”** / **„Miért fordul el jobban a kanyar belső ívén futó első kerék?”** [Victoria route copy and mechanism explanation](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/stops/victoria/car.js:8)

### UX findings

1. **Land visitors at the room picker.** On both tested screen sizes, tapping “See the route” put the first room at the top of the screen and the entire picker above it. Someone already standing in Legend 6 would have to know to scroll backwards. Point the homepage button and the highlights’ “See the full route” link to the existing room navigation. “Find your room” / „Teremválasztás” would make the destination clear. [Route page](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/index.html:28) · [Highlights link](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/teaser.html:31)
2. **Give the SLK phase labels enough room.** On the emulated iPhone, „Csomagtartófedél fel” occupied 112 px in a 76 px cell. It also overflowed the iPad’s side panel. After the prompt has named the boot lid, „Fedél nyílik” and „Fedél zárul” are enough. A two-column layout would give the other phases room to wrap. [iPhone screenshot](/private/tmp/museum-copy-review.ONZgcf/phone-roof.png) · [Phase labels](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/lib/app/i18n/hu.js:530)
3. **Carry the experiment through a language switch.** After selecting the lowered 300 SL frame, switching languages restored the original frame and returned me to the top. A visitor checking an unfamiliar Hungarian term loses the comparison that gave it meaning. Preserve the active section and selected option. [Language switch](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/lib/app/i18n.js:39)
4. **Give more route cards a question worth opening.** Only three of the 46 have a visitor question and a cue for where to look. I’d start with the other two highlights, since many visitors will meet them first. The Blitzen-Benz already has a ready-made experiment: “If you double the power, do you double the speed?” / „Ha megduplázza a teljesítményt, a végsebesség is a kétszeresére nő?” [Blitzen-Benz exhibit](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/stops/blitzen-benz/hu.js)

### Two exhibit descriptions to correct

- **300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé.** The highlights introduction calls the exhibit “the most expensive car ever sold”. Mercedes-Benz built two and sold the other one. A short replacement in both languages would be “One of two Uhlenhaut Coupés. Its twin sold for €135 million in 2022.” / „A két Uhlenhaut Coupé egyike. A másik példány 2022-ben 135 millió euróért kelt el.” [Highlights introduction](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/teaser.html:30) · [Mercedes-Benz sale announcement](https://group.mercedes-benz.com/company/news/uhlenhaut-coupe.html)
- **O 302 football coach.** Both versions identify the vehicle as the bus that carried West Germany’s team. Daimler Truck identifies the exhibit as a replica. I’d say “A replica of West Germany’s 1974 World Cup team bus” / „A nyugatnémet válogatott 1974-es világbajnoki csapatbuszának másolata”. Its location also deserves a check before visitors rely on it. The tour sends them to Collection 1, while Daimler Truck’s exhibit photo identifies Collection 4. [Tour entry](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/stops/o302/car.js:9) · [Daimler Truck exhibit description](https://www.daimlertruck.com/en/newsroom/pressrelease/maximum-bus-comfort-for-the-1974-world-cup-footballers-52102483)
Make an .md file with the proposals.
I’ll save the proposals in `docs/`, with the English and Hungarian wording side by side and links to the pages each change affects.

# Museum tour wording and visitor experience

*Review of 25 November 2026, revision `636d7a4`. The review covered all 46 route cards in English and Hungarian. The route, highlights and selected exhibit interactions were checked in WebKit using iPhone 15 and iPad Pro 11 emulation. Gallery locations still need on-site confirmation.*

## Fix two obstacles on the visitor’s path

1. **Take visitors to the room picker.** Tapping “See the route” placed the first room at the top of the screen. The entire room picker was already above it on both devices. A visitor standing in Legend 6 would have to scroll backwards to discover the shortcut. Label the homepage button **Find your room** / **Teremválasztás** and link it to `#jump`. Point “See the full route” on the highlights page to `./#jump` as well. Check that following either link brings the room choices into view, including on a fresh page load. [Route](../index.html) · [Highlights](../teaser.html) · [Room picker](../lib/app/index.js)

2. **Make every SLK roof phase readable.** The Hungarian label *Csomagtartófedél fel* needed 112 px in a 76 px phone cell. It also overflowed the 81 px cell on the iPad in landscape. The prompt already identifies the boot lid, so the opening sequence can use **Fedél nyílik** and **Fedél zárul**. Use two columns when four labels cannot fit. Check the closing sequence too, so the highlighted wording describes the movement the visitor sees in either direction. [Roof controls](../subsystems/vario-roof.js) · [Hungarian labels](../lib/app/i18n/hu.js) · [Panel layout](../lib/app/theme.css)

## English and Hungarian copy

| Location | What gets in the way | Proposed English | Javasolt magyar szöveg |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 540 K route card | In “when did it join in?” and “mikor lépett működésbe?”, the nearest subject is the letter K. | What does the K stand for? When does the supercharger kick in? | Mit jelent a K betű? Mikor kapcsol be a kompresszor? |
| 300 SL frame comparison | “Lecsökkentve szokásos ajtókhoz” leaves out what was lowered. Visitors can see the sill change height. | Original high sill / Lower sill for conventional doors | Eredeti, magas küszöb / Alacsony küszöb hagyományos ajtóhoz |
| SLK roof prompt | “Watch the steps light up” draws attention to the indicators. In Hungarian, “a lépések kigyulladnak” can suggest catching fire. | Tap “Open the roof”. Which moves first, the boot lid or the roof? | Koppintson a „Tető nyitása” gombra. Mi mozdul meg először, a csomagtartó fedele vagy a tető? |
| Simplex gearbox legend | “Pair in mesh” leaves the parts unnamed. “Kapcsolódó kerékpár” can be read as a bicycle. | Gears in mesh | Kapcsolódó fogaskerekek |
| Offline instructions on the route and highlights | “With signal” and “térerővel” suggest mobile reception even on Wi-Fi. Opening the page starts the download. The ready message tells visitors when they can disconnect. | Open the tour while you’re online. When you see “Ready offline”, every stop is saved on this device. | Nyissa meg a túrát, amíg van internetkapcsolata. Amint az oldal jelzi, hogy a túra offline is elérhető, internet nélkül is megnyithatja bármelyik megállót. |
| Offline confirmation | “Offline is kész” sounds unfinished. Use the same wording in the instructions and the confirmation. | Ready offline. All stops are saved on this device. | A túra offline is elérhető. Az összes megálló mentve van a készüléken. |
| Benz Victoria route card | Both versions say the front wheels follow the same circle. The inner wheel follows a tighter arc, and the model shows the two steering angles. | Why does the inner front wheel turn more sharply? | Kanyarodáskor miért fordul el jobban a belső első kerék? |

The exhibit wording lives with the cars. Gear labels and offline messages are shared across pages. [540 K](../stops/540k/hu.js) · [300 SL](../stops/300sl/hu.js) · [SLK](../stops/slk/hu.js) · [Victoria](../stops/victoria/car.js) · [Gearbox](../subsystems/gearbox.js) · [Offline status](../lib/app/offline.js) · [Hungarian UI text](../lib/app/i18n/hu.js)

## Keep visitors oriented during an experiment

- **Preserve the comparison when switching languages.** On the 300 SL, selecting the lowered frame and switching languages restored the original frame and returned the page to the top. Someone looking up an unfamiliar term loses the example that explains it. Keep the active mechanism and selected setting in view. A practical check is to switch EN → HU → EN at the lowered frame and see the same comparison each time. [Language switch](../lib/app/i18n.js) · [Scroll story](../lib/app/story.js)
- **Give the other two highlights a question and a visual cue.** Three of the 46 route cards already pair a visitor question with something to find at the exhibit. On the Blitzen-Benz, try **“If you double the power, do you double the speed?”** / **„Ha megduplázza a teljesítményt, a végsebesség is a kétszeresére nő?”** Have visitors compare the two speeds using the existing power slider. [Blitzen-Benz](../stops/blitzen-benz/car.js) · [300 SLR](../stops/300slr/car.js)

Verify the room separately. The tour lists Collection 1, while Daimler Truck’s 2022 exhibit photographs are captioned Collection 4. [English exhibit text](../stops/o302/car.js) · [Hungarian exhibit text](../stops/o302/hu.js) · [Route placement](../stops/tour.js) · [Daimler Truck exhibit description and photographs](https://www.daimlertruck.com/en/newsroom/pressrelease/maximum-bus-comfort-for-the-1974-world-cup-footballers-52102483)

content.text: Both Evo II body choices use the same CFD silhouette, and that silhouette leaves out the rear wing. I also traced the camshaft readout to six engine configurations that draw no separate camshaft. I’ll cover both in the proposal and distinguish what the model omits from what the real engine used.

changes.diff:
@@ -34 +34,41 @@
 **O 302 football coach.** The route card, photo description and exhibit text identify the displayed vehicle as the coach that carried the team. Daimler Truck identifies it as a replica. Use **“A replica of West Germany’s 1974 World Cup team bus”** / **„A nyugatnémet válogatott 1974-es világbajnoki csapatbuszának másolata”** wherever visitors first encounter it. Verify the room separately. The tour lists Collection 1, while Daimler Truck’s 2022 exhibit photographs are captioned Collection 4. [English exhibit text](../stops/o302/car.js) · [Hungarian exhibit text](../stops/o302/hu.js) · [Route placement](../stops/tour.js) · [Daimler Truck exhibit description and photographs](https://www.daimlertruck.com/en/newsroom/pressrelease/maximum-bus-comfort-for-the-1974-world-cup-footballers-52102483)
+
+## Evolution II — put the racing bodywork in the wind tunnel
+
+Klaus Ludwig’s number 3 DTM car is the reason to open this stop. The visitor can pick out the wing above the boot, the lip below the front bumper and the flared arches around the tyres in the exhibit photo. Yet both body buttons feed **the same solid shape** to the flow solver. The wing appears in the outline but is omitted from the CFD profile, the underside is flat, and the wheels lie outside the centre plane. Switching bodies changes the road-car drag and top-speed calculation. It cannot show what those three parts do to the air. Move the autobahn comparison into the background as road-car context. [Exhibit photo](../stops/190e-evo2/photo.jpg) · [Evo II configuration](../stops/190e-evo2/car.js) · [How the tunnel is selected](../subsystems/aero.js)
+
+**Open at a fast corner.** Ask **“Why would a racing driver accept more drag?”** / **„Miért éri meg a versenyzőnek a nagyobb légellenállás?”** Start at one fixed speed with the wing selected. Highlight the part on the photo, then show the same part close up in the flow. One tap changes one piece of geometry. Keep the camera, speed and colour scale fixed so the visitor can see what changed.
+
+| Part and visitor action | What to reveal in the CFD | What it means on track |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| **Rear wing · Hátsó szárny.** Extend the adjustable upper flap. Keep the lower strip and roof-edge spoiler fixed. | Show the pressure on both wing surfaces, the flow arriving from the rear window, and the wake. Put a downward arrow at the wing and a rearward arrow for drag. Let their lengths follow the calculated forces. | Extra rear aerodynamic load can give the rear tyres more grip in a fast bend. Extra drag costs speed on the following straight. The two arrows make the price of the adjustment visible. |
+| **Front splitter · Első légterelő lemez.** Switch the front lip between its two longitudinal positions. | Zoom to the nose at road level. Show where air meets the upper face and where it passes under the lip. Compare the change in front aerodynamic load alongside rear load, with the wing setting held fixed. | A driver needs the front tyres to turn the car as well as the rears to hold their line. Moving aerodynamic load forward can help when the front runs wide in a fast bend. |
+| **Flared fender · Kiszélesített sárvédő.** Compare the flared arch with a reference contour that clears the same tyre. Label the reference as an experiment. | Use a view across the front wheel and a velocity slice just behind it. Trace the flow that passes around the tyre shoulder and rejoins the body side. Hold tyre width, wheel position, rotation and ride height fixed. | The flare accommodates the wheel. Its shape also changes the disturbed air the rest of the car encounters. Let the measured change in this model determine what the caption says about drag. |
+
+The FIA’s Evo II homologation extension **A-5269, 29/02 ES**, sheets 5–7, gives photographs and drawings of the front lip, upper and lower rear flaps, roof-edge spoiler and cylinder head. Use them with the number 3 photo to establish geometry. Mercedes-Benz documents the front lip’s two positions and the extendable upper flap on the homologation car. Identify the proposed settings as comparisons wherever the 1992 race setup is unknown. Wheel-arch experiments also show why the wheel position must be controlled when comparing fenders. [FIA Group A homologation form](https://historicdb.fia.com/sites/default/files/car_attachment/1601062201/homologation_form_number_5269_group_a.pdf) · [Mercedes-Benz on the adjustable aero package](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/4e61dcd8-fd75-47ca-830c-056734a165c2) · [Rotating-wheel and wheelhouse experiment](https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/12/17/3340)
+
+**Compute four cases ahead of time.** For this stop, use one simplified 3D car, a moving road and rotating wheels. Solve a baseline plus one change per part. Export just the pressure and velocity slices, a few streamlines and mean force differences for the existing stage to display offline. The fender needs lateral flow, which the live side-view solver cannot resolve. For front and rear load, derive the axle reactions from the whole-body vertical force and pitching moment about a known reference. The force on the wing alone does not give the rear axle load. Show relative changes in the exhibit and identify them as results for the simplified model. [Existing flow solver](../lib/model/flow.js) · [Wind-tunnel rendering](../lib/scene/wind-tunnel.js)
+
+**Pilot the wing first.** Resolve the flap and its gap in the computational mesh. Check that the direction of the averaged load and drag changes survives mesh refinement before writing the takeaway. Repeat that check for the lip and fender. If the fender’s drag difference is smaller than the numerical uncertainty, show the change in its wake and leave the drag delta unreported. On an offline iPhone, each switch should reveal a visible difference at the selected part, with a text description that also works with motion reduced. A visitor should be able to explain why a team might choose different settings for two circuits.
+
+## Evolution II — give the racing engine one short experiment
+
+**Yes, the 2.5-litre four is worth a second step.** It earns its place by showing how little time a racing cylinder has to fill. Mercedes-Benz specifies a 97.8 mm bore and 82.8 mm stroke for the race engine. The early DTM version produced 245 kW at 8,500 rpm and could reach 9,500 rpm. The figure quoted for the 1992 championship car is **up to 274 kW (373 PS)**. The road Evo II had a 97.3 mm bore and produced 173 kW (235 PS). Keep each power figure attached to its version. The source gives the early engine’s maximum speed separately from the 1992 power figure. [Mercedes-Benz on the road and race engines](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/25dd00e4-5ef9-4c2f-b12c-55169f795d4d)
+
+Ask **“At 9,000 rpm, how long does one cylinder have for its intake stroke?”** / **„Percenként 9000-es fordulatszámnál hány ezredmásodpercig tart a szívóütem?”** Let the visitor switch between 4,500 and 9,000 rpm while watching one cylinder in slow motion. The crank turns through the intake stroke in **6.7 ms and 3.3 ms** respectively. Highlight the two inlet valves opening together and trace the piston down the short bore stroke. Two inlet valves give the charge a larger opening to pass through in that brief interval. Put the real elapsed time beside the picture. These times describe 180° of crank rotation. Actual valve opening extends over a different interval determined by cam timing.
+
+Reuse the four-stroke animation and show **two camshafts and four valves per cylinder** before inviting visitors to count them. The current generic DOHC view draws one inlet and one exhaust valve per cylinder. The FIA head photograph on sheet 7 gives the model a visual reference. Use a slow-motion time scale and a pause control so visitors can follow one cam revolution through two crank revolutions. Put power figures in the supporting text. The useful result of the experiment is the time available to breathe. [Engine renderer](../subsystems/inline-engine.js) · [Four-stroke timing](../lib/model/engine.js) · [FIA cylinder-head photograph, extension 29/02 ES](https://historicdb.fia.com/sites/default/files/car_attachment/1601062201/homologation_form_number_5269_group_a.pdf)
+
+## Camshafts — match each explanation to the engine on screen
+
+The shared piston-engine panel always creates and updates a **Camshaft / Vezérműtengely** angle by dividing crank angle by two. Six of its 19 configured engines draw no separate camshaft. Other stops do draw a shaft but leave out the link to the valve. These cases need different edits. [Panel, drawing and update logic](../subsystems/inline-engine.js)
+
+| Stops | What the model and text say today | Proposed correction |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Benz Patent-Motorwagen | The valve gear is omitted in the drawing. A camshaft angle still runs. Mercedes-Benz describes an intake slide and a controlled exhaust valve on the real engine. | Remove the camshaft readout and its per-frame update for this view. Keep the crank angle. Describe the pictured piston and flywheel, and identify any discussion of the actual valve gear as background. [Stop configuration](../stops/patent-motorwagen/car.js) · [Mercedes-Benz on the original engine](https://group.mercedes-benz.com/company/tradition/company-history/1885-1886.html) |
+| Daimler stationary engine, Reitwagen, motor carriage, Marie motorboat and Benz Velo | All five use the atmospheric-inlet drawing. It shows a moving exhaust rod and a suction-operated inlet. The panel labels a separate half-speed shaft. The Daimler engine story describes a groove driving the exhaust. | Show the intake opening as the piston descends. For the documented Daimler drive, highlight the groove, follower and exhaust rod when those parts are depicted. Verify the exhaust drive for each variant, especially the Benz Velo, before reusing that description. Use the crank or stroke indicator for timing. [Daimler engine stop](../stops/daimler-engine/car.js) · [Velo stop](../stops/velo/car.js) · [Mercedes-Benz on the Daimler exhaust drive](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/article/f37c559a-5986-4a7a-ab64-6fc195752b99) |
+| 190 SL and engines with visible shafts | The 190 SL introduction says the cam opens the valve “directly”. The factory workshop manual shows a rocker arm between the cam and valve. The shared overhead-cam drawing leaves that rocker out. At the Simplex 60 stop, the text itself records that its side exhaust valve is drawn overhead. | Correct the 190 SL wording in both languages and show one complete cam–rocker–valve path in close-up. On the Simplex 60, focus on the documented overhead inlet and distinguish the side exhaust in the cutaway. At other shaft-equipped stops, check the default view for the part the visitor is asked to watch. [190 SL wording](../stops/190sl/car.js) · [Workshop manual, fig. 01-4/20a](https://s3cf792cad773e861.jimcontent.com/download/version/1612462948/module/15676396822/name/Mercedes%20Benz%20Service%20Manual%20180%20to%20220SE.pdf) · [Simplex 60 geometry note](../stops/simplex-60/car.js) |
+
+**First repair:** derive readout visibility and updates from the same valvetrain configuration that draws the shaft. For the Daimler engine, use **“Watch the inlet open as the piston moves down.”** / **„Figyelje meg, hogyan nyílik ki a szívószelep, amikor a dugattyú lefelé indul.”** For the corrected 190 SL cutaway, use **“Follow the cam as it presses the rocker arm and opens the valve.”** / **„Figyelje meg, hogyan nyomja le a bütyök a szelephimbát, és hogyan nyílik ki a szelep.”**
+
+Check all 19 configurations for agreement between the drawing, readout and both languages. Exercise at least one view each with omitted gear, atmospheric inlet, pushrods, a single overhead cam and twin overhead cams. A shaft-equipped model should show one shaft revolution per two crank revolutions. In a view with omitted gear the crank and piston should still run with the cam readout absent. For every “watch” prompt, pause at the opening stroke on a phone and check that the named part and what it moves are both identifiable.

content.text:
I added three proposals to the [museum tour review](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/docs/bilingual-copy-and-ux-proposals.md:36), with English and Hungarian visitor prompts.

1. **Make the Evo II’s bodywork the CFD experiment.** Both current body choices use the same airflow silhouette, and it omits the rear wing. I’d replace the top-speed demonstration with three comparisons at a fixed speed. Extend the rear wing flap to see the trade between rear grip and drag. Move the front splitter to see how aerodynamic load shifts between the axles. Then look across the rotating front wheel to see how the flared fender changes its wake. Precomputed 3D flow would make all three comparisons available offline. The FIA drawings provide a reference for the actual parts. [Aero proposal](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/docs/bilingual-copy-and-ux-proposals.md:36) · [FIA homologation form](https://historicdb.fia.com/sites/default/files/car_attachment/1601062201/homologation_form_number_5269_group_a.pdf)

2. **The 2.5-litre racing engine deserves a short second step.** At 4,500 rpm, one intake stroke takes **6.7 milliseconds**. At 9,000 rpm, it takes **3.3**. Let visitors switch between those speeds while watching two inlet valves open together in slow motion. That gives the sixteen-valve head a purpose they can see. Mercedes-Benz quotes up to **274 kW (373 PS)** for the 1992 championship car. [Engine proposal](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/docs/bilingual-copy-and-ux-proposals.md:54) · [Mercedes-Benz engine figures](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/25dd00e4-5ef9-4c2f-b12c-55169f795d4d)

Give the **300 SL** the balance experiment, the **770** the firing-pulse comparison and the **W 196 R** the historical engineering decision. The moving pistons exert reactions on the engine block and its mounts. Within each cylinder, the primary inertia force repeats once per crank revolution. The connecting rod’s changing angle introduces a secondary component that repeats twice. In the tour’s symmetric, equal-mass six- and eight-cylinder layouts, the first- and second-order forces and their rocking moments cancel in the sum. The crankshaft still receives torque pulses at different positions along its length, and the driveline carries the resulting fluctuating torque. [Engine kinematics](../lib/model/engine.js) · [Reciprocating forces and engine balance](https://www.epi-eng.com/piston_engine_technology/forces_on_recip_components.htm)

| Stop | What the visitor does and sees | Discussion prompt |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **300 SL Gullwing · Straight-six balance** | Pause the existing engine and step through a revolution. Show a force arrow along each cylinder, then their sum and the rocking moment about the engine midpoint. Pistons 1 and 6 move together. Add the other two pairs and watch the total cancel. Switch between the once-per-revolution and twice-per-revolution components. The 190 E’s conventional inline-four makes a useful comparison because its secondary forces add. | “How can six moving pistons leave the engine balanced?” / „Hogyan egyenlítik ki egymás tehetetlenségi erőit a soros hathengeres dugattyúi?” |
| **770 · Straight-eight firing pulses** | Keep the existing firing animation and put a torque trace at the crank output. At the same 3,000 rpm, an evenly firing four-stroke six has three firing pulses per revolution (150 per second), and an evenly firing eight has four (200 per second). Highlight each firing cylinder as its pulse reaches the trace. Compare at equal mean torque so visitors can distinguish pulse spacing from engine power. | “Can you still pick out the individual power strokes at the output?” / „A főtengelyen leadott nyomaték görbéjén felismerhetők az egyes munkaütemek?” |
| **W 196 R · Crankshaft resonance** | After the aero story, show the two groups of four cylinders and the gear that takes power from the middle of the crankshaft. Mark the front, centre and rear of the shaft with witness lines. Sweep engine rpm and watch the relative twist grow near a torsional natural frequency. Let visitors compare the actual centre take-off with an illustrative end take-off under the same firing input and load. Trace the torque path to the propeller shaft and rear transaxle. | “Why did Mercedes take the drive from the middle of the crankshaft?” / „Miért a főtengely közepéről hajtották meg a hátsó kerekeket?” |

The W 196 R makes the distinction tangible. Taking power from the middle gives each four-cylinder group a shorter path to the output gear. Mercedes-Benz records vibration as a reason for that choice. Resonance is a separate observation in the model: when a repeated torque input excites a natural twisting mode, the relative angle can grow even while the engine remains externally balanced. Offer a damping control to see the resonance peak diminish. Label it as a model experiment. [300 SL engine](../stops/300sl/car.js) · [770 engine](../stops/770/car.js) · [Mercedes-Benz archive on the M 196 centre drive](https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/Mercedes-Benz-W-196-R-streamlined-racing-car-1954.xhtml?oid=6873) · [Measured six-cylinder crankshaft response with and without a damper](https://saemobilus.sae.org/papers/experiment-computation-analyses-torsional-vibration-crankshaft-system-viscous-torsional-damper-diesel-engine-1999-01-1748)

**Model and proof.** Reuse the existing crank angles, cylinder positions, stroke and rod length for the balance arrows. Use real rpm for the calculations and slow motion for the picture. For torsion, connect front, centre and rear crank inertias with elastic, damped segments and couple the chosen output to a driveline load. Plot relative angle along the **crankshaft / főtengely** and transmitted torque in the **propeller shaft / kardántengely**. Mark exaggerated twist, assumed stiffness, damping, inertias and firing inputs as illustrative. Exact M 196 firing phases and critical speeds need period evidence before they can be attributed to the car.

Check the force and moment sums through a full revolution, and check pulse counts across a full 720° firing cycle. In the torsion model, hold excitation amplitude fixed and compare steady-state twist below, near and above resonance, then repeat with more damping. A visitor should be able to pause on a balanced force display and a fluctuating torque trace and explain why both can be true.

# Mercedes-Benz Museum technical tour

Static GitHub Pages site: one page per exhibit showing its mechanism working (three.js), offline after one visit, for
iPhone/iPad Safari (iOS 16.4+, import maps). No bundler: native ES modules; `tools/build.mjs` only stamps the service worker.

## Map
- `index.html` route (lib/app/index.js) · `stop.html?s=<slug>[&r=teaser]` one stop as a scroll story (lib/app/shell.js;
  r=teaser pages among the teaser stops and links back to teaser.html): the car's stage pins while its steps (intro on the
  photo, one per component with its cards, background with the outline) scroll past and set what it shows ·
  `teaser.html` the three `teaser` stops' stories one after another (lib/app/teaser.js, own manifest) · `sw.js` offline
  cache (new root files also go in tools/build.mjs ENTRIES)
- `stops/tour.js` route order, room, level, `check` ("room" or "level": not yet confirmed on site, shown as a qualifier),
  and `teaser` (slugs): single source for order and prev/next ·
  `stops/<slug>/car.js` pure data (+ photo.jpg) · `parts/` real-life photos of mechanisms the exhibits hide (component `real`; shared
  between stops)
- `lib/model/` pure maths, Node-tested: linkage (multi-link closure), quarter-car (ride), engine (N-cylinder slider-crank,
  timing, diesel), blower, valvetrain (spring float, desmo), steering (double-pivot trapezoid, centre pivot, twin steered
  axles), differential (one axle; traction4: four-wheel drive with locks or brake traction control), gearbox (sliding
  gears), aero (drag, top speed), truss (space frame twist), crash, air-spring (levelling: air, or a motor-wound torsion
  bar), wankel, cooling, belt (two-speed flat-belt drive, hill climbing), hoist (car-transporter deck: cylinder, pulley
  block, cables), flow (2-D lattice-Boltzmann wind tunnel: D2Q9 + Smagorinsky, moving road, drag split), abs (tyre slip
  curves, braking with and without ABS), rollover (tip angle, rolling pendulum, roll-bar timing), hydraulics (gas
  accumulator, pump, cylinders), climate (cabin heat balance), portal (portal-axle clearance), roof (folding hardtop)
- `lib/scene/` stage (renderer, cameras, lights, theme tokens, loop), helpers, ghost-body, road, wind-tunnel (CFD view of
  `flow` on the centre plane: speed/pressure/swirl field, body section, smoke streaklines; `--cfd-*` tokens)
- `lib/app/` shell, teaser, story (scroll stories: shared by shell and teaser), viewer (one car's stage, subsystems,
  photo view and loop: one per story), panel
  (declarative widgets, API in its header; `detail: true` on a card or widget moves it under the step's disclosure when
  the component has `more`), dom (`h`, `link`), offline, index, theme.css (look after
  mercedes-benz.com: black bar/hero, white page, condensed serif, black photo cards, pills), fonts/ (Instrument Serif, OFL;
  latin + latin-ext for ő/ű), lang.js (head script: saved EN/HU choice or browser language → `<html lang>`), i18n.js
  (`t`, `num`, `loadCar`, `localizePage`), i18n/hu.js (UI catalog keyed by the English text)
- `subsystems/<id>.js` one mechanism each (params documented in each file's header): linkage-suspension, inline-engine,
  roots-blower, desmo-valvetrain, steering, differential, gearbox, radiator, aero, space-frame, crumple-zone,
  air-suspension, wankel, belt-drive, hoist, abs, rollover, comfort-hydraulics, cabin-climate, portal-axle,
  four-wheel-drive, twin-steer, vario-roof. inline-engine also draws V engines (`leans`: one bank per lean angle,
  opposite cylinders sharing a crankpin) and twin ignition (`plugs: 2`); crumple-zone can carry an engine block that
  slides under the floor (`engine`)
- `tools/` build, vendor-three, camera (shared pinhole maths), fit-photo-camera (+ photo-fits/*.json), trace-profile
  (+ profile-traces/*.json: side-photo pixels → mm profile), photo-grid (crop + pixel grid + projected profile overlay, PNG
  via Playwright), stop-shot (stage screenshot + fps + page errors; needs `npm run serve`) · `docs/TOUR-POC.md` (model maths §6), `docs/research.md`
- `vendor/three/` is generated by `npm run vendor -- <version>`: never read or edit it.

## Conventions
- Vehicle frame: mm in configs, metres in the scene; x forward, y left, z up; origin per car in `frame.origin`. z = 0 is
  axle height for the first six cars, the ground for the rest: each car.js header says which.
- Camber − = top inboard · toe + = toe-in · travel + = bump · steer + = left.
- Colours only through CSS tokens (`stage.bind`, `stage.tokenMat`, `var(--…)` in SVG): never hard-code theme colours.
  `--band`/`--card` are the fixed-black areas (header bar, index hero, stop cards) and stay dark in both themes.
- Illustrative numbers get a comment in car.js and a line in `unverified` (the page shows it). Sources go in `sources`.
- Panel DOM is built with textContent only; widget ids must be unique within a component.
- English is the source; Hungarian is complete and tested. UI text: `t("English literal", ...args)` with `{0}` placeholders
  (never a variable or template as the key; whole phrases, as Hungarian case endings differ), static HTML: `data-i18n`.
  Logic never compares displayed text: keep English keys/ids and map them to `t(...)` for display. Readout numbers pass
  through `num` (decimal comma). Car text: `stops/<slug>/hu.js`, car.js's shape with only the text fields (list in
  tests/unit/helpers.mjs `TEXT`), null keeps the original; sources and credits stay untranslated.

## Contracts
- car.js: `{ slug, title, name, year, summary, question?, eyebrow, lede, look?, takeaway?, frame?, ride?, orbit?, sun?,
  body?: { ghost }, photo?: { …, caption? }, components: [{ id, label, subsystem, view: { pos, target }, ghost?: { fill, edge },
  params, talk, prompt?, answer?, more?, real? }], note, unverified, sources }`. `question` replaces the summary on the index
  card; `look`/`takeaway` open and close the story at the car; a component with `prompt` shows prompt → key controls →
  `answer`, and `more` names the disclosure holding the detail widgets and the facts (piloted on 300sl, slk, 540k). `real:
  { src: "parts/<x>.jpg", w, h, alt, caption, credit }` shows the part in real life after the answer, only where the
  exhibit hides it (under the body or bonnet): any car's, ~800 px wide, free licence, caption saying whose it is.
- Subsystem: `export function create(ctx, params)` with ctx `{ stage, carRoot, frame, ride, panel, reducedMotion, t }`, returns
  `{ layout({ active, onPhoto }), update(dt, { onPhoto }) }`. lib/app/viewer.js owns photo view, outline, ghost body and
  the loop (the story's step at the reading line chooses what it shows; a car without a photo shows its model), and
  resets carRoot's pose each frame before calling the active component's `update`.

- Add a stop: entry in `stops/tour.js` + `stops/<slug>/car.js` (copy the closest sibling). Photo (every stop has one): 1200 px
  wide, CC licence with credit, camera fitted with `node tools/fit-photo-camera.mjs tools/photo-fits/<slug>.json` (wheel
  centres and tyre bottoms first; `focalPrior` when the points are nearly flat). Trace `body.ghost` from the photo so Car
  outline lines up. Subsystems fade their own opaque wheels and keep the body still when `onPhoto`. Tests find it via tour.js.
  Add `stops/<slug>/hu.js` (npm test lists missing text fields) and, for a new room, its name in `lib/app/i18n/hu.js`.
- Add a mechanism: `lib/model/<x>.js` + `tests/unit/<x>.test.mjs` first, then `subsystems/<x>.js`.
- Wind tunnel for an aero stop (every aero stop has one; Blitzen-Benz is the worked example; a shape may carry its own `profile`):
  find a near-square side photo (Commons) → `tools/photo-fits/<slug>-side.json` (wheel hubs, tyre tops/bottoms/fronts/rears;
  `focalPrior` as the points are coplanar) → read outline pixels off `node tools/photo-grid.mjs <photo> <out.png> x0 y0 x1 y1
  3 10` → `tools/profile-traces/<slug>.json` (each group on its plane y) → `node tools/trace-profile.mjs` → clean up into
  `body.ghost` (silhouette) and the aero component's `flow.profile` (centre-plane section: round sharp noses, which separate
  at this low Reynolds number; add a driver for open cars) → check both with `photo-grid --overlay` on the stop photo →
  `npm test` (flow tests run every `flow` config for stability). Keep the tunnel near 16k cells (iPhone budget).
- Upgrade three.js: `npm run vendor -- <version>` (a release at least two weeks old), then `npm test && npm run e2e`.

## Commands
- `npm test` unit tests (models, configs, translations) · `npm run e2e` Playwright: WebKit iPhone/iPad × 4 (Hungarian pass on
  iPhone only) and Chromium offline (builds first)
- `npm run serve` dev server on :8765 (service worker off on localhost unless `?sw=1`) · `?debug` exposes `window.__tour`
- `npm run build` → `_site/` · deploy: push to main; `.github/workflows/pages.yml` tests, then deploys.

## Real-device checklist (iPhone and iPad Safari, from the Pages URL)
Portrait and landscape · light and dark · EN/HU switch · stop pages and teaser: each stage stays pinned while its steps scroll · orbit, pinch, sliders · photo overlay lines up with Car outline on · airplane mode
after one visit: index → every stop · Add to Home Screen, launch offline · iPad Split View · Low Power Mode still animates at

+

Use the tour’s existing tap-to-enlarge control so visitors can switch between the metal part and the animation in the same space. The Roots blower already shares one period illustration across three stops, and the 190 E uses a Toyota axle to explain its suspension. Both patterns suit this tour. [Existing part images](../parts/) · [Photo interaction](../lib/app/story.js) · [190 E example](../stops/190e/car.js)

+| **1899 Daimler van · tubular radiator.** Crop Valder137’s original exhibit photograph around the round face and starting crank (CC BY 2.0). The outer face locates the cooler. Maybach’s 1897 sectional drawing shows what lies behind it. [Exhibit photograph](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Daimler_Motor-Gesch%C3%REDACTED%2814983294032%29.jpg) · [Maybach’s drawing](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tubular_car_radiator_copy_of_patent_drawing.png) | “Where does the air go after it enters the front of the radiator?” / „Merre áramlik tovább a levegő a hűtő belsejében?” Keep the starting crank visible as a landmark, then follow one air tube in section. Switch to the plain tank and see where air can reach its metal walls. |
+| **300 SLR · desmodromic valves.** Gérard Delafond’s close-up looks through the inspection opening of a Ducati motorcycle engine. The upper rocker touches the valve tip and the fork beneath it catches the collar. CC BY-SA 3.0. [Ducati valve gear](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Desmo_photo.jpg) | “Which rocker pulls the valve shut?” / „Melyik himba húzza vissza a szelepet?” Mark the two contact points. Pause the Mercedes animation as the valve closes and find the contact that carries the load. The shared feature is mechanical closing. The Ducati photograph shows its own rocker layout. |
+| **600 Pullman · hydraulic accumulator.** Nutzdatenbegleiter’s sectioned Citroën suspension sphere exposes the thick rubber diaphragm and the spaces on either side. CC BY-SA 4.0. [Citroën sphere in section](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cit-hydraulic-accumulator.jpg) | “What pushes the oil out while the pump is idle?” / „Mi nyomja ki az olajat, amikor a szivattyú áll?” Label gas, diaphragm and oil on the photo. Raise the 600’s rear window with the accumulator charged and watch the pressure drop. The Citroën uses the gas cushion in its suspension. The Mercedes uses stored pressure to move the window. |
+

+

+| **260 D · diesel prechamber.** Gwafton’s photo shows a sectioned 1934 Ganz–Jendrassik diesel cylinder head. Credit the Hungarian engine by name and mark the small chamber and its outlet. content.text:
I added **seven real-world image pairings** to the [proposal document](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/docs/bilingual-copy-and-ux-proposals.md:123), each with an image source, an English and Hungarian visitor question, and a specific detail to find in the animation.

I’d start with three:

- **1899 Daimler van.** Find the round radiator and starting crank on the exhibit photo, then follow one tube in Maybach’s drawing. The animation can show air passing through the tube, water flowing around it, and why a plain tank sheds less heat. [Cooling proposal](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/docs/bilingual-copy-and-ux-proposals.md:110)
- **300 SLR.** A Ducati engine close-up shows the forked rocker beneath the valve collar. Ask visitors to find the part that **pulls the valve shut**, then watch it act in the Mercedes animation. [Ducati valve gear](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Desmo_photo.jpg)
- **600 Pullman.** A cut-open Citroën suspension sphere exposes the rubber diaphragm. Visitors can see how compressed gas pushes oil out, then raise the Mercedes’s rear window and watch the stored pressure fall. [Citroën sphere](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cit-hydraulic-accumulator.jpg)

The other four pairings cover the **260 D diesel prechamber, 300 SL straight-six crankshaft, Benz Velo belt controls, and SLK folding roof**. Each proposed caption identifies the donor vehicle or engine where known.
